A theoretical comparison between autoregressive (AR) and masked (MLM) pretraining reveals distinct trade-offs depending on the downstream task [2407.00935].

*   **Classification Tasks:** Masked pretraining generally outperforms autoregressive pretraining. Theoretically, this is because masked SSL allows for more flexibility in choosing target tokens, which fosters stronger inter-sample connections compared to the fixed-position target tokens used in autoregressive SSL. This leads to superior clustering performance [2407.00935].
*   **Content Generation Tasks:** Autoregressive pretraining is better suited for generation. Masked SSL suffers from a misalignment between the variable lengths of test samples and the fixed length of unmasked texts used during training, which hinders its generative performance. In contrast, autoregressive models naturally accommodate the flexible lengths of conditional texts [2407.00935].

To address these limitations, it is possible to improve model performance by incorporating diversity-enhanced autoregressive objectives or variable-length masked objectives [2407.00935].
